newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's hustle to price mark bond pays off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's hustle to price mark bond pays off.

text.p: Brazil's hustle to place its 10-year 500 million Deutsche mark ($305 million) bond on Tuesday paid off with a better-than-expected launch price of 230 basis points over the equivalent German Bund, traders said.

"Brazil had to do it this week to make sure they would get good market conditions. They were able to get it done in one or two days," said a trader at a large international bank in Brazil that participated in the syndicate.
He added that there was strong demand for the issue, which was Brazil's first trip to international capital markets this year.

The market, which thought Brazil might not place the issue for another week or two, had expected the bond to price wider than the 265-b.p. spread on its $750 million 8-7/8 global bond due 2001. But rushing it to market while there was still plenty of demand for high-yielding emerging market paper was seen as a key factor for the success of the deal, traders said.
"Our quick swap calculations put (the 230-b.p. Bund spread) at about 250 basis points over 10-year U.S. Treasuries which is tighter than we expected," said a trader at a Brazilian investment bank.
He added that pricing of the bond ahead of Federal Reserve Board's Federal Open Market Committee Tuesday and Wednesday also supported the strong launch price.
A U.S. interest rate hike, thoughly unlikely, would make it much more expensive to borrow on world capital markets, he said.
Traders said the issue remained well bid at 230 b.p. over after its launch.
Despite a lower credit rating, Brazil's 10-year mark bond came in at a tighter spread than Mexico's 12-year 1.5 billion mark bond, which priced Tuesday at 260 b.p. over.

Market watchers said the pricier Brazilian issue was due to its smaller size and the fact that Brazil has only one other issue in Deutsche marks - a three-year 1.0 billion mark bond priced in June 1995 - which gave the new issue rarity value.
Brazil did not begin seeking bids for the deal until Jan 23 and it did not name CS First Boston as lead manager until last Thursday, an official at the bank said.

Market players said Brazil had learned a lesson about timing following the lukewarm reception of its global bond last November. Brazil decided to launch a global in mid-September when the market was well bid for emerging market paper.
But by the time the bond priced a month later, the market was oversupplied and the issue quickly traded down to 290 b.p. over after pricing at 265 b.p. over.
